summary: xAI added a 'workflows' feature to Grok Build that lets the agent plan a task, fan it out across up to 1,024 parallel background agents, verify results, and return a single report.

mechanisms.reason: The feature explicitly runs many agents in parallel and autonomously to completion, the definition's 'agents running autonomously at scale' case.
mechanisms.quote: orchestration scripts that fan a task out across hundreds of parallel agents, verify the results, and report back in one background run.

mechanisms.reason: A single task now spawns hundreds to over a thousand agent calls instead of one conversation turn, multiplying tokens issued per task.
mechanisms.quote: Runs get a budget of 128 agents, and up to 1,024 for big jobs.

practices.reason: The multi-phase fan-out-and-verify pattern (context, review, adversarial verification, synthesis) is a concrete agent orchestration design an engineering team could study, though it is delivered as xAI's own tool rather than a portable recipe.
practices.quote: Grok plans the task as a small script: the phases of work, the agents in each phase, and how their results roll up. Each agent starts with a clean, focused context, and the plan can build in checks a single pass can't, like independent skeptics verifying every finding before it reaches the final report.
